title: Kapoor Singh Receives the Robe of Honor

blocks.text: The Khalsa resolves the matter by choosing Kapoor Singh, not because he has sought office, but because the Panth recognizes service, endurance, and courage in him. The congregation presents the robe of honor to Kapoor Singh as a collective decision rather than as an imperial appointment imposed from above.

The elevation raises the public standing of the Khalsa. Mughal officials now speak more carefully, payments and concessions begin to flow, and the arrangement gives Lahore a temporary way to reduce pressure while acknowledging a power it cannot simply crush.

Even so, the political balance remains sharp. Aslam Khan treats the settlement as a tactic that may buy time, while the Singhs use the moment to strengthen their own position, gather at Guru Chak, and expand the prestige of the Panth.
